title: The holy calling
summary: Alma tells his brethren that the Lord God ordained priests after the order of his Son to teach the people, so they might know how to look forward to his Son for redemption.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord God ordained priests after his holy order, which was after the order of his Son, to teach the people.
The priests were ordained in a manner intended to help the people know how to look forward to his Son for redemption.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma addresses a group of brethren.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and the audience's appearance.
The visual arrangement of the speakers and listeners.

narration.text: the Lord God ordained priests, after his holy order
the people might know in what manner to look forward to his Son for redemption.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses refer to the priests' ordination and its purpose; they do not narrate a particular ordination ceremony.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting a specific ordination ceremony.
Visibly depicting the Son or giving him an appearance not stated in these verses.

title: Called and prepared
summary: Those called had chosen good and exercised great faith. Others would reject the Spirit of God because of the hardness of their hearts and blindness of their minds.

explicit_facts.text: Those ordained were called and prepared according to the foreknowledge of God, on account of their exceeding faith and good works.
They were left to choose good or evil; they chose good and exercised exceedingly great faith.
Others would reject the Spirit of God on account of the hardness of their hearts and blindness of their minds; otherwise they might have had as great privilege as their brethren.

unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's identity and appearance.
The setting and appearances of the people discussed.

narration.text: they having chosen good, and exercising exceedingly great faith
others would reject the Spirit of God on account of the hardness of their hearts and blindness of their minds

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses teach about choice and calling; they do not narrate a present scene.
prohibited_inventions: Identifying the speaker as Alma from these verses alone.
Depicting a premortal selection or a visible manifestation of the Spirit.
Staging the reported choices and callings as a present event.

title: The holy calling and high priesthood
summary: The verses describe the holy calling, ordination to the high priesthood, and the purpose of teaching God's commandments.

explicit_facts.text: They were on the same standing with their brethren.
The holy calling was prepared from the foundation of the world for those who would not harden their hearts, in and through the atonement of the Only Begotten Son.
Those called were ordained to the high priesthood of the holy order of God to teach his commandments to the children of men, that they might enter into his rest.

unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearances of those called and their brethren.
Any physical setting or ordination ceremony.

narration.text: thus this holy calling being prepared from the foundation of the world for such as would not harden their hearts, being in and through the atonement of the Only Begotten Son, who was prepared—
to teach his commandments unto the children of men, that they also might enter into his rest—

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses teach about a calling and its purpose; they do not narrate a visible ordination or describe the appearance of a divine figure.
prohibited_inventions: A named speaker or audience.
A specific ordination ceremony.
A visible depiction of the atonement or the Only Begotten Son.

title: Without beginning or end
summary: Alma describes the priesthood as eternal and its holders as high priests forever after the order of the Son.

explicit_facts.text: The high priesthood is after the order of the Son, prepared from eternity to all eternity, and without beginning of days or end of years.
Those ordained take upon them a calling, ordinance, and high priesthood described as without beginning or end.
They become high priests forever after the order of the Son, who is full of grace, equity, and truth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma's teaching continues as off-screen speech.
unspecified_visual_details: Any symbolic visual design for eternity or the priesthood.

narration.text: prepared from eternity to all eternity
they become high priests forever, after the order of the Son

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Eternal duration is a teaching, not a literal visible scene.
prohibited_inventions: Invented heavenly imagery or depictions of the Son.

title: Faith and repentance
summary: Many were ordained and became high priests of God because of their faith, repentance, and righteousness. They were called after the holy order and sanctified; many were made pure and entered the rest of the Lord their God.

explicit_facts.text: Many were ordained and became high priests of God on account of their faith, repentance, and righteousness; they chose to repent and work righteousness rather than perish.
They were called after the holy order and sanctified; their garments were washed white through the blood of the Lamb.
After being sanctified by the Holy Ghost, they were pure and spotless before God and could not look upon sin without abhorrence; many entered the rest of the Lord their God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching can be presented without depicting the people or actions it describes.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearances of the high priests.
The setting and identity of the speaker.
Any visible form for sanctification or the Lord's rest.

narration.text: there were many who were ordained and became high priests of God;
Therefore they were called after this holy order, and were sanctified, and their garments were washed white through the blood of the Lamb.
there were many, exceedingly great many, who were made pure and entered into the rest of the Lord their God.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses describe the high priests retrospectively; they do not narrate a present ordination, washing, or entry into rest.
The garment-washing language does not establish a visible washing ceremony.
prohibited_inventions: Identifying the speaker as Alma from these verses alone.
Staging a present ordination or literal washing ceremony.
Depicting blood, wounds, or an invented appearance of divine figures.

title: An appeal to humble yourselves
summary: A speaker calls his brethren to humble themselves before God and bring forth fruit meet for repentance so they may enter into rest. He cites the people in Melchizedek's days, describes Melchizedek's high priesthood, and says Abraham paid Melchizedek tithes.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker calls his brethren to humble themselves before God and bring forth fruit meet for repentance so they may enter into rest.
The speaker urges them to humble themselves as the people in Melchizedek's days did.
Melchizedek was a high priest after the order the speaker has discussed and took upon him the high priesthood forever.
Abraham paid Melchizedek tithes of one-tenth of all he possessed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The speaker may be shown addressing listeners, without specifying their appearance or the setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's and listeners' appearances.
The location and its appearance.
The circumstances and appearance of Abraham's tithe payment.

spoken_dialogue.text: who also took upon him the high priesthood forever.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

spoken_dialogue.text: yea, even our father Abraham paid tithes of one-tenth part of all he possessed.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Melchizedek and Abraham are mentioned in the speaker's teaching, not described as present.
prohibited_inventions: Identifying the speaker as Alma from these verses alone.
Showing Melchizedek or Abraham in a newly staged event.
Depicting rest or repentance as a literal supernatural event.

title: Ordinances point to the Son of God
summary: Ordinances were given so the people might look forward to the Son of God for remission of their sins and enter the rest of the Lord.

explicit_facts.text: The ordinances were given as a type of the Son of God's order so the people might look forward to him for remission of their sins and enter the rest of the Lord.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching can be presented without depicting a particular ordinance.
unspecified_visual_details: The ordinances' appearance or performance.
The appearance of the Son of God.

narration.text: that they might look forward to him for a remission of their sins, that they might enter into the rest of the Lord.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse explains the ordinances' purpose; it does not narrate a particular ordinance being performed.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting an unspecified ritual or visibly showing the Son of God.
Assigning this verse's words to a named speaker.

title: Melchizedek Preaches to His People
summary: Melchizedek, king over Salem, preached repentance to his people, who had gone astray. They later repented, and he established peace in the land.

explicit_facts.text: Melchizedek was king over the land of Salem, and his people had gone astray.
Melchizedek exercised mighty faith, received the office of the high priesthood according to the holy order of God, and preached repentance to his people.
His people repented; he established peace in the land in his days, was called the prince of peace, and reigned under his father.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Melchizedek may be shown addressing a group of his people while preaching.
unspecified_visual_details: Melchizedek's appearance, the people's appearances, and the setting's architecture.

narration.text: did preach repentance unto his people.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Keep the depicted moment focused on preaching; repentance and the establishment of peace are subsequent outcomes, not simultaneous visible actions.
The verses give no words from Melchizedek's sermon.
prohibited_inventions: Invented sermon dialogue or a specific conversion episode.
A visible appearance by Melchizedek's father.
A fabricated event showing how peace was established.

title: A warning about the scriptures
summary: An unidentified speaker says many came before and after an unnamed man, but none were greater. The speaker says the scriptures are before the addressees and warns against wresting them.

explicit_facts.text: Many were before and after the unnamed man, but none were greater; he was mentioned more particularly.
The speaker says the scriptures are before the addressees and warns that wresting them will be to their destruction.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The speaker addresses others, though their appearance is not described.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's identity and appearance.
The addressees' number and appearance.
The setting and the physical form, if any, of the scriptures before the addressees.

spoken_dialogue.text: Now I need not rehearse the matter; what I have said may suffice. Behold, the scriptures are before you; if ye will wrest them it shall be to your own destruction.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

narration.text: Now, there were many before him, and also there were many afterwards, but none were greater; therefore, of him they have more particularly made mention.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The destruction warning is teaching, not a depicted event.
prohibited_inventions: Identifying the speaker or the unnamed man from outside these verses.
Depicting destruction or inventing a scripture-reading event.

title: Alma calls for repentance
summary: After speaking to them, Alma stretched forth his hand and cried with a mighty voice.

explicit_facts.text: Alma had said words unto them before stretching forth his hand.
Alma stretched forth his hand unto them and cried with a mighty voice.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma faces those he addresses with his hand extended.
unspecified_visual_details: Alma's appearance, the audience's size, and the surroundings.

title: Glad tidings declared
summary: The voice of the Lord, by the mouth of angels, declares glad tidings to all nations, including people scattered abroad. The tidings have come to the speaker’s group and are made known to them in plain terms.

explicit_facts.text: The voice of the Lord, by the mouth of angels, declares glad tidings to all nations, including people scattered abroad.
The tidings have come to the speaker’s group and are made known to them in plain terms.
The speaker describes the group as wanderers in a strange land and says glad tidings are declared to them in all parts of their vineyard.

reasonable_visual_inferences: An unidentified person could be shown speaking; the angelic declaration is reported rather than narrated as a present appearance.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker’s appearance and immediate setting.
The identities and appearances of the angels and scattered people.

And they are made known unto us in plain terms, that we may understand, that we cannot err;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The angelic declaration is reported teaching, not a separately narrated present event.

title: Preparing hearts
summary: Alma says angels are declaring the message to many in their land to prepare hearts for the Son's coming, which they await.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says angels are declaring the message to many in their land to prepare people's hearts to receive the Son's word at his coming in glory.
Alma says they wait for joyful news of the Son's coming, whose time they do not know, and he wishes it might be in his day.
Alma says he will rejoice whether the coming is sooner or later.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma's words continue off-screen over the audience's setting; the coming is anticipated, not depicted.
unspecified_visual_details: The angels, the people who hear them, and the Son's appearance.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The future coming is anticipated in speech, not shown.

title: Made known at his coming
summary: The verse foretells that something will be made known to just and holy men by the mouth of angels at the time of his coming, so that the fathers’ words concerning him may be fulfilled.

explicit_facts.text: Something shall be made known to just and holy men by the mouth of angels at the time of his coming.
The fathers spoke concerning him according to the spirit of prophecy, and their words may be fulfilled.

unspecified_visual_details: No location or physical appearance is described.

narration.text: And it shall be made known unto just and holy men, by the mouth of angels, at the time of his coming, that the words of our fathers may be fulfilled, according to that which they have spoken concerning him, which was according to the spirit of prophecy which was in them.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The disclosure is foretold, not narrated as occurring in this verse.

title: Do not procrastinate
summary: Alma urgently urges his hearers to repent, humble themselves, pray continually, and have faith, hope, and love.

explicit_facts.text: Alma wishes with great anxiety that his hearers heed him, cast off their sins, and not procrastinate repentance.
He urges them to humble themselves, call on God's name, watch and pray continually, and be led by the Holy Spirit into humility, meekness, patience, love, and long-suffering.
He urges faith in the Lord, hope of eternal life, and love of God, so they may be lifted up at the last day and enter his rest.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma urgently addresses the audience; his counsel can remain off-screen speech.
unspecified_visual_details: The audience's reactions and any actions they take in response.

narration.text: cast off your sins, and not procrastinate the day of your repentance
watch and pray continually

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage gives counsel, not a narrated scene of the audience praying.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting the audience acting on the counsel or showing the last day.

title: Alma's concluding prayer
summary: Alma asks the Lord to grant the people repentance and protect them from wrath, the chains of hell, and the second death; he speaks more words that are not written.

explicit_facts.text: Alma asks that the Lord grant the people repentance so they will not bring down his wrath, be bound by the chains of hell, or suffer the second death.
Alma spoke many more words to the people, which are not written in the book.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma remains before the audience as he concludes; the written account does not specify the content of his additional words.
unspecified_visual_details: The wording of Alma's additional words and the audience's response.

narration.text: may the Lord grant unto you repentance

prohibited_inventions: Inventing the unrecorded words or depicting hell, chains, or the second death.
